'''Wolpe''': {{legend0|#7996e2|50–60%}} | title = [[Governor of Michigan|Governor]] | before_election = [[John Engler]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[John Engler]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsMI}} The '''1994 Michigan gubernatorial election''' was held on November 8, 1994, to elect the [[Governor of Michigan|Governor]] and [[Lieutenant Governor of Michigan|Lieutenant Governor]] of the state of [[Michigan]]. Incumbent Governor [[John Engler]], a member of the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican Party]], was re-elected over [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]] nominee and [[Congressman]] [[Howard Wolpe]]. The [[voter turnout]] was 45.5%.{{Cite web |url=http://michigan.gov/sos/0,4670,7-127-1633_8722-29616--,00.html |title=General Election Voter Registration/Turnout Statistics |publisher=State of Michigan official website |access-date=December 13, 2011 |archive-date=December 22, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111222230957/https://www.michigan.gov/sos/0,4670,7-127-1633_8722-29616--,00.html |url-status=live }} ==Republican primary== ===Candidates=== *[[John Engler]], incumbent Governor ===Campaign=== Engler, who was narrowly elected in [[1990 Michigan gubernatorial election|1990]], ran unopposed in the Republican primary{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1994/08/04/us/victors-in-michigan-primaries.html |title=Victors in Michigan Primaries |work=New York Times |date=August 4, 1994 |access-date=October 15, 2017 |archive-date=October 15, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171015151420/http://www.nytimes.com/1994/08/04/us/victors-in-michigan-primaries.html |url-status=live }} and retained Lt. Lynn Jondahl]], State Representative from [[Okemos, Michigan|Okemos]] *Larry Owen, former mayor of [[East Lansing]] and former member of the [[Michigan State University]] Board of Trustees *[[Debbie Stabenow]], State Senator from [[Lansing, Michigan|Lansing]] *[[Howard Wolpe]], former U.S. Representative from [[Lansing, Michigan|Lansing]] ===Campaign=== All four candidates were notably from [[Lansing, Michigan|Lansing]] or its immediate surroundings.
